# Docs and ADR rules

## The documents
- `docs/design/design.md` is the design: philosophy, syntax, decision record (section 8),
  experiments (section 9), internal architecture (section 10), test strategy (section 11). It is
  the plan, too: section 9 checklists are ticked as experiments finish. Korean translation:
  `design-KO.md` (the language rule applies).
- `docs/architecture.md` describes what **exists now** (packages, layers, enforcement). Keep it
  true; when code changes the picture, update it in the same change.
- `docs/spikes/NNNN-*.md` record experiments (`run-spike` skill).
- `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` record decisions taken **after** the design document.

## When an ADR is needed
For a decision that is expensive to reverse and is not already in the design document's decision
record: public API shape, supported versions, a guard or layer change, a dependency, a change of a
section 8 decision, anything that bends a design invariant. Small, local, easily reversed choices
need no ADR - explain them in the commit body.

## ADRs are lightweight
An ADR exists so the maintainer can read it and be convinced. That is the whole bar.
- Short: Context (facts, links), Decision, Consequences, and the alternatives that were seriously
  considered (one or two lines each). Template: `docs/adr/0000-template.md`. Add evidence (spike
  write-up, test, measurement) when the decision rests on a fact that could be wrong.
- Status: `Proposed` -> `Accepted` (or `Rejected`, or `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`). An agent writes
  `Proposed`; it becomes `Accepted` only when the maintainer says so (in the conversation or the PR
  review) - then write `Accepted (maintainer, <date>)`. Agents never accept an ADR themselves.
- Asking the `architect` sub-agent for a review is recommended for cross-layer decisions, not
  required.
- **Amending** is fine in place while the decision keeps its direction: edit the text and append
  one line to the `History` section (`<date> - what changed`). If the direction reverses, write a
  new ADR that supersedes the old one.
- Code may be written against a `Proposed` ADR on a work branch; the PR is not merged until the
  maintainer has accepted it.
- When an ADR changes or adds to a design decision, update `docs/design/design.md` (and its
  translation) in the same change, and link the ADR from the affected section.
